title: Lolo and the Too Much Honey
moral: Too much of anything is not good; balance is important.

scenes.summary: Lolo the bear loves honey but eats too much of it.
scenes.text:
Lolo the Bear Who Ate Too Much Honey

In a sunny forest filled with tall trees and buzzing bees, lived a little bear named Lolo.

Lolo loved honey more than anything.

Sweet, sticky, golden honey—yum!

But there was one problem…

Lolo loved it a little too much.
scenes.image_prompt: cute bear happily eating honey near beehive in sunny forest, colorful cartoon style

scenes.summary: Lolo ignores advice and keeps eating more honey than he should.
scenes.text:
Every day, Lolo visited the beehive.

“Just a little honey,” he said.

But “a little” became a lot.

And a lot became too much!

“Lolo, be careful,” said Mimi the Deer.

“Too much honey is not good.”

But Lolo just laughed.

“I love honey!” he said.
scenes.image_prompt: bear eating lots of honey while deer looks concerned, bright forest cartoon scene

scenes.summary: Lolo eats too much honey and feels sleepy and unwell.
scenes.text:
One day, Lolo ate more honey than ever.

Big scoops!

Sticky paws!

Full tummy!

Soon, Lolo felt very tired.

“I feel… sleepy,” he mumbled.

He lay down under a tree.

And fell fast asleep.
scenes.image_prompt: bear lying under tree sleeping with honey pot nearby, soft cartoon style

scenes.summary: Lolo realizes he missed fun and learns about balance from Tina.
scenes.text:
While Lolo slept, his friends played.

They ran, jumped, and laughed.

But Lolo missed it all.

When he woke up, the sun was setting.

“Oh no!” he said.

“I missed everything!”

Just then, Tina the Tortoise walked by.

“Why are you sad?” she asked.

“I ate too much honey,” Lolo said.

“And I missed all the fun.”

Tina nodded.

“Too much of anything can be a problem,” she said.
scenes.image_prompt: sad bear watching sunset while friends play in distance and tortoise talks kindly, cartoon style

scenes.summary: Lolo learns moderation and enjoys both honey and playtime.
scenes.text:
The next day, Lolo went to the beehive.

“Just a little,” he said.

He took a small taste.

And stopped.

Then he went to play with his friends.

Lolo ran, laughed, and had fun all day.

“I feel great!” he said.

“And I didn’t miss anything!”

Too much of anything is not good.

Balance makes life better.

The End

story:
Lolo the Bear Who Ate Too Much Honey

In a sunny forest filled with tall trees and buzzing bees, lived a little bear named Lolo.

Lolo loved honey more than anything.

Sweet, sticky, golden honey—yum!

But there was one problem…

Lolo loved it a little too much.

Every day, Lolo visited the beehive.

“Just a little honey,” he said.

But “a little” became a lot.

And a lot became too much!

“Lolo, be careful,” said Mimi the Deer.

“Too much honey is not good.”

But Lolo just laughed.

“I love honey!” he said.

One day, Lolo ate more honey than ever.

Big scoops!

Sticky paws!

Full tummy!

Soon, Lolo felt very tired.

“I feel… sleepy,” he mumbled.

He lay down under a tree.

And fell fast asleep.

While Lolo slept, his friends played.

They ran, jumped, and laughed.

But Lolo missed it all.

When he woke up, the sun was setting.

“Oh no!” he said.

“I missed everything!”

Just then, Tina the Tortoise walked by.

“Why are you sad?” she asked.

“I ate too much honey,” Lolo said.

“And I missed all the fun.”

Tina nodded.

“Too much of anything can be a problem,” she said.

The next day, Lolo went to the beehive.

“Just a little,” he said.

He took a small taste.

And stopped.

Then he went to play with his friends.

Lolo ran, laughed, and had fun all day.

“I feel great!” he said.

“And I didn’t miss anything!”

Too much of anything is not good.

Balance makes life better.

The End
